title: geo-aware shredding layer and cryptographic erasure receipts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers and regulators need provable, region-aware deletion semantics: when a tenant requests erasure we must ensure data is destroyed in the correct legal region, record an immutable, compact proof of deletion, and provide a developer-facing API and UI for verification. Current flows rely on asynchronous job logs and DBA-run manual checks that do not produce a tamper-resistant, compact artifact suitable for audits.

Goal: Implement a 'shredding layer' that enforces geo-residency during purge runs and emits cryptographic erasure receipts (compact signed proofs) per-request. Deliver a REST API and console view to fetch and validate receipts and an automated reporter for compliance exports. The receipts should support offline verification by customers and auditors without exposing PII.

Out of scope: full legal attestation workflow involving external notaries, long-term archival of raw logs beyond retention policy, automated legal hold resolution (handled by separate legal-hold ticket).
scope_items: Implement region-aware purge worker that tags resources with residency metadata and triggers per-region shredding actions
Design a compact cryptographic receipt format (signed statement, deletion-checksum, region stamp, epoch) and a verification endpoint
Console: per-request receipt viewer and bulk export for a tenant with filtering by date and region
API: POST /deletion-requests/{id}/verify -> returns receipt and verification status
Integrate receipts into existing audit export pipeline (S3 manifest + signed bundle)
success_metrics: Receipts generated for >= 95% of customer-initiated erasure requests within 10 minutes of job completion
Verification endpoint returns deterministic validated=true/false in < 200ms for cached receipts
Reduction in manual support escalations for deletion evidence by 80% in Q2
Compliance export bundles pass internal audit checklist in staging run
acceptance_criteria: For a staged tenant with multi-region residency, perform deletion request that results in region-specific shredding tasks and generation of a signed receipt per region
Receipt payload contains deletion-checksum, region tag, timestamp, and signing key id; signature verifies with Redwood public key
Console shows receipt and a human-readable summary; export bundle contains per-request receipts and a manifest.json
API verification endpoint validates signature and returns reason codes for failure modes (missing-region, checksum-mismatch, signature-invalid)
Integration test that replays a previously-completed deletion and proves verification fails after a simulated tamper of receipt
design_considerations: Receipt privacy: do not include raw PII; include deterministic deletion-checksums derived via salted hash with tenant-scoped salt stored in KMS
Key management: use KMS-backed signing keys; rotate keys with key id versions included in receipts
Compactness: receipts should be small (< 4KB) to enable embedding in emails and exports; include optional compressed proofs for large job bundles
Replayability: include an immutable epoch and sequence id so auditors can order deletions without exposing user identifiers
Region failure modes: when a region is down, emission of a 'pending' receipt with a retry policy and an eventual 'completed' receipt replacing it
engineering_risks: Race between asynchronous purge jobs and receipt emission could cause transient mismatches; needs atomic commit pattern or idempotent design
KMS signing latency could add to completion time; mitigation: pre-warmed ephemeral signing tokens or batched signing
Cross-region consistency: ensuring deletion truly occurred in the locality claimed requires careful scheduling and observability ties to underlying infra
Receipt verification performance under high query load (console/bulk exports) — may need caching and shard-aware verification
